#### `contractHash`

function · `import { contractHash } from '@harness/sdk'`

The hash an approved install binds its pairing grant to (`Hello.contractHash`): the manifest's contract parts, the same
whether worked out from the contract alone (fs's build, before anything runs) or by the running system. What only the
process adds is left out: its client assets, the events its implementation handles, whether it serves resources, and
its context, which may come from its context folder (all inside the approved bundle, whose hash fs checks).

```ts
function contractHash(manifest: Manifest): Promise<string>;
```

Refers to: [`Manifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.manifest#core-manifest).

#### `ManifestOptions`

interface · `import { ManifestOptions } from '@harness/sdk'`

What the serve runtime adds to a contract to make its manifest.

```ts
interface ManifestOptions {
  /** The system's version (its package version). */
  version: string;
  /** Hub events its implementation handles. */
  events?: readonly SystemEventType[];
  /** Whether its implementation serves resources. */
  resources?: boolean;
  client?: ClientAssets;
  /**
   * The instance this process is: a runtime provider (`provider({ models: 'runtime' })`) is sent named after it, with
   * `runtimeModels` (the models the running system set). Without one, the manifest has no runtime provider.
   */
  instance?: InstanceName;
  runtimeModels?: readonly ProviderModelDecl[];
}
```

Refers to: [`InstanceName`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-instancename), [`ProviderModelDecl`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.system-providers-ts#core-providermodeldecl).

#### `ProviderServer`

class · `import { ProviderServer } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

Serves `providerChat`, `providerEmbed`, `providerDecide` and `providerModels` with the system's own aeye providers.

```ts
class ProviderServer {
  constructor(parts: ProviderServerParts);
  /** Stream a chat call: the provider's chunks, then the usage it reported. */
  chat(data: ProviderChat, signal: AbortSignal): AsyncGenerator<ProviderChunk>;
  /**
  * Embed inputs with an embedding model of a provider: aeye's one `inputs` list when it has images, else its `texts`
  * shorthand (so a text-only provider reading `texts` keeps working). An image is an http(s) or data URL, which every
  * aeye provider reads as an `EmbeddingImage`.
  */
  embed(data: ProviderEmbed, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ProviderEmbedResult>;
  /** Answer questions about an input with a decision model of a provider (aeye's `decide`). */
  decide(data: ProviderDecide, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ProviderDecideResult>;
  /**
  * The declared models a provider serves now, from its aeye `listModels`, with the limits it serves them with; a
  * provider that can't list says so (`listed: false`), and the hub then offers every declared model.
  */
  models(data: ProviderModels): Promise<ProviderModelsResult>;
}
```

#### `ProviderServerParts`

interface · `import { ProviderServerParts } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What the provider server needs.

```ts
interface ProviderServerParts {
  /** The contract's provider declarations by local name. */
  readonly defs: Readonly<Record<string, ProviderDef>>;
  /** The implementation's provider factories by local name. */
  readonly impls: Readonly<Record<string, (ctx: SystemCtx) => Provider>>;
  /** The system context now, on the system's own signal (throws when there is no valid config). */
  readonly ctx: () => SystemCtx;
  /** The current config version; a provider is made again when it changes. */
  readonly configVersion: () => number | undefined;
  /** The contract's runtime provider, if it has one: its local name, this instance's name and its models now. */
  readonly runtime?: { readonly local: string; readonly instance: () => string; readonly models: () => readonly ProviderModelDecl[] } | undefined;
}
```

Refers to: [`ProviderModelDecl`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.system-providers-ts#core-providermodeldecl).

#### `KeyStore`

interface · `import { KeyStore } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

A system's signing key pair, kept in its state folder.

```ts
interface KeyStore {
  /** The public key (Ed25519, SPKI DER, base64), making the pair on first use. */
  publicKey(): Promise<string>;
  /** Sign a challenge nonce. */
  sign(nonce: string): Promise<string>;
  /** The auto-pair secret the hub granted, if any, to re-pair with when the hub doesn't know this key. */
  autoPair(): Promise<AutoPairGrant | undefined>;
  /** Keep the newest grant (each welcome may rotate it), or forget it (`undefined`) once the hub refused it. */
  saveAutoPair(grant: AutoPairGrant | undefined): Promise<void>;
}
```

Refers to: [`AutoPairGrant`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.auto-pair-ts#core-autopairgrant).

#### `scrubbedEnv`

function · `import { scrubbedEnv } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The environment a supervised child gets: from `base`, only `PATH`, the OS basics (`BASIC_ENV`) and the SDK
tunables (`SHARED_ENV`), never the parent's identity, keys or anything else, then `extra` on top.

```ts
function scrubbedEnv(base: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>, extra?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): Record<string, string>;
```

#### `BASIC_ENV`

const · `import { BASIC_ENV } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The OS variables a child keeps (matched without case, as Windows names them `Path`, `SystemRoot`, ...).

```ts
const BASIC_ENV: readonly ["PATH", "SYSTEMROOT", "TEMP", "TMP", "TMPDIR"];
```

#### `SHARED_ENV`

const · `import { SHARED_ENV } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The harness variables a child inherits, by name: the SDK runtime tunables (`sdkEnv`: link timing, log level, ...),
never the parent's instance identity. An explicit list, not a `HARNESS_` prefix, so a parent's own settings and
secrets (the hub's admin password, signing and encryption keys) never reach a child.

```ts
const SHARED_ENV: readonly string[];
```
